title: Finite reduction of the Poincare pairing
statement:
Use the smooth Poincare setting, with
the admissible structure morphism and normalized smooth orientation.
Let $n\geq m\geq1$, put $A_n=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ and
$A_m=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^m$, and let $K_n$ be a
site-perfect constructible
$A_n$-complex. Put $K_m=K_n\otimes^L_{A_n}A_m$.
The coefficient comparisons identify the reduction of the
derived Poincare pairing
for $K_n$ with the pairing for $K_m$. In particular, writing
$K_n^\vee$ for its coefficient dual,
the canonical isomorphisms make the square

$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
R\Gamma_c(X,K_n)^\vee\otimes^L_{A_n}A_m
&\xrightarrow{\beta_{K_n}^{\sharp,-1}\otimes1}&
R\Gamma(X,K_n^\vee(d))[2d]\otimes^L_{A_n}A_m\\
\downarrow\wr&&\downarrow\wr\\
R\Gamma_c(X,K_m)^\vee
&\xrightarrow{\beta_{K_m}^{\sharp,-1}}&
R\Gamma(X,K_m^\vee(d))[2d]
\end{array}
$$

commute. Here $\beta^{\sharp,-1}$ denotes the inverse of the
tensor–Hom adjoint of the pairing.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sf-pod-smooth-dual-reduction-data]. At both stages $K_i$ and $L_i=K_i^\vee(d)[2d]$ are site-perfect bounded constructible finite-Tor complexes; $F_XL_n\cong L_m$ preserves evaluation, orientation and the trace contractions $\tau_i$. Write $F_T=\operatorname{red}_T$, $C_i=R\Gamma_c(X,K_i)$ and $D_i=R\Gamma(X,L_i)$.

source.place: First paragraph: reduction models, dual, evaluation and trace.

proof.text: Use [prop-sf-mixed-cup-coefficient-change] for $A_n\to A_m$, $K_n,L_n$. Write its canonical compact-support comparison as $c:F_sC_n\xrightarrow{\sim}C_m$ and its ordinary comparison, followed by $R\Gamma(X,F_XL_n\cong L_m)$, as $r:F_sD_n\to D_m$. Its square states $c_{K_n\otimes L_n}F_s(\smile_{c,n})=\smile_{c,m}(c\otimes r)$ with tensor comparisons understood. Only this equality is needed here. Compose it with the contraction comparison from step 1. The definition [def-pod-derived-poincare-pairing] is $\beta_i=\tau_i\smile_{c,i}$, so $F_s(\beta_n)=\beta_m(c\otimes r)$ under $F_sA_n\cong A_m$.

source.place: Second paragraph: cup square composed with evaluation and trace.

proof.text: By [thm-pod-point-perfectness], $C_n,C_m$ are perfect point complexes. Apply the point internal-Hom and evaluation clauses of [lem-fix-operation-reduction] to obtain the evaluation-compatible isomorphism $h:F_s(C_n^\vee)\xrightarrow{\sim}(F_sC_n)^\vee$. By [thm-pod-identification-of-the-comparison], the pairing adjoints $b_i:D_i\xrightarrow{\sim}C_i^\vee$ are isomorphisms: step 1 supplies perfectness of both $K_i$. Apply [lem-sf-perfect-pairing-reduction-adjoints] to $F_s$, $\beta_n,\beta_m,c,r,h$ and the pairing identity of step 2. It gives $\ell=(c^{-1})^\vee h$, $b_mr=\ell F_s(b_n)$, and $rF_s(b_n^{-1})=b_m^{-1}\ell$, and proves $r$ invertible. The last identity is the stated square, with its canonical left comparison $\ell$ and right comparison $r$. All reductions are derived; the perfectness invoked is that of $C_n$, not flatness of $A_m$ over $A_n$.

source.place: Second paragraph: point perfectness, inverse-adjoint square and invertibility of the ordinary comparison.

proof_origin.place: Three-step assembly of the two new lemmas and the existing mixed-cup coefficient-change theorem.

\begin{array}{ccc}

R\Gamma(X,K_n^\vee(d))[2d]\otimes^L_{A_n}A_m\\

proof.text:
The compact-support, tensor, site-perfect internal-Hom and evaluation
comparisons are [lem-fix-operation-reduction]. Thus the coefficient dual of
[def-pod-coefficient-dual-on-x], the cup product and evaluation
in [def-pod-derived-poincare-pairing], and their adjunction maps
all reduce compatibly. The remaining geometric ingredient is the
normalized trace of [def-pur-smooth-trace]; its coefficient
compatibility, together with that of the smooth orientation, is
[thm-pur-finite-reduction-of-purity].
The identification in [thm-sf-dual-perfect] uses
that orientation and the same internal-Hom operations.
Composing these commuting squares gives the square for the pairing,
using the canonical coefficient comparison on ordinary global sections;
no isomorphism assertion for that map is needed at this step.
By [thm-pod-point-perfectness] the compact-support complex is
perfect, so its coefficient dual commutes with reduction and the left
vertical map is an isomorphism. For each admissible coefficient ring,
[thm-pod-identification-of-the-comparison] identifies the adjoint
of the pairing with the duality isomorphism. Taking adjoints in the
commuting pairing square therefore proves that the ordinary-global-section
comparison on the right is an isomorphism too. Taking inverses of the
horizontal adjoints gives exactly the displayed square.
No flatness of $A_m$ over $A_n$ is asserted: every reduction is
derived, and the coefficient-dual comparisons use the stated
perfectness hypothesis.
